evidence.title: Locally adaptive control processes can undermine system-level safety in a conceptual model
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: Rasmussen models legislators, organizations, planners and operators as interacting control processes. Local adaptation to commercial pressures can move activity toward unsafe system boundaries. Observation period and measurement context: Conceptual synthesis; no fixed observation interval.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; Conceptual engineering analysis; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition

source_locations.SRC-133: Accepted manuscript abstract, introduction, PDF pp. 10–14 and Figures 4–6

evidence.limitations: Historical conceptual and engineering argument with illustrative cases, not a controlled AI experiment or prevalence estimate. Recommendations are normative. Does not establish that contemporary AI environments meet the Commons hypothesis.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: A conceptual antecedent for describing distributed adaptation; not evidence of the Commons term’s actual origin.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Distributed adaptive control environment
terms.definition: A proposed characterization of interacting human, organizational, and AI activities in which participants with distinct objectives continuously influence one another’s information, actions, and relationships. Its usefulness is descriptive; the scope and consequences of such environments require investigation.

relationships.explanation: Provides a conceptual antecedent; does not empirically establish the contemporary Commons hypothesis.
